reason: This text passage (Exodus 1-7) depicts the Israelites expressing distress and suffering through groaning (נְאָקָה) and crying out (שׁוְעָה) due to their bondage in Egypt, but does not show them explicitly voicing criticism against their leaders or Yahweh. Instead, their cries are directed toward God as petitions for deliverance (וַתַּעַל שַׁוְעָתָ֛ם אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים). The text does show the Israelites failing to listen to Moses due to their despair, but this is not characterized as voicing criticism. Moses expresses doubt to God about his own adequacy, but this is not the Hebrew people criticizing their leaders or God.
